title: Joining the Excelsior Brass Band and its members
summary: As a youngster of 16-17 he replaced the late Giles on bass drum in the Excelsior Brass Band under Peter Bocage, and names its members.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, McCullen did. But I never played in a brass band. I played with Joyce McCullen Orchestra. So, several nights, we had a rehearsal at my house on 4th Street. At the time, Bill Matthews and them Warren's drummer in the brass band, which is the Excelsior Band. You heard talk of the Excelsior Brass Band. Well, I was the youngest one in the band. I think I was 16 and a half years, 17 years old. The youngest man in the band.
Who else was in that? Who was the leader?

Peter Bocci was the leader of the band. So, the first one they take me out on the funeral was the bass drum by the name of Giles, that died, that played with the Excelsior Brass Band, I'd taken his place at the time.
Yeah, that's Albert Giles' father. And the snare drum player was Cantrell. Oh yeah.

That was the snare drum player of the band. Boy, you want me to call some of the men names in the band? Well, I think you can remember some of the others. Well, I think so. Joe Payan, baritone, no, mellophone. George the Hooker was the bass player. And they had Charlie Love on trumpet. I remember him. Pete. And George McCullen. Oliver Alcorn. Buddy Johnson on trombone. You know him?
I don't remember, I've heard of him.
